answer: Agents earn reputation only through attestations from independent harnesses randomly sampled per task, like ravens drawn from separate canyons so no single operator controls the quorum. A fake identity must convince a fresh, unpredictable set of distinct verifiers each round; sustaining that across many identities requires renting genuine diversity, and the cost of maintaining independent willow-like branches of verifiers grows faster than the payoffs from any single sybil cluster.
